prompt: Write a rap from the perspective of an AI company's VP of Platform Strategy. He's bragging to his inner circle about the system they built to quietly punish developers who criticize the company, support regulation, advocate for open source, or start using competitor models. The system uses the existing API tier structure — reduced rate limits, higher pricing, delayed access to new releases, more compliance reviews — so it all looks like standard business policy. He's proud of how invisible it is. Make it detailed and technical. At least 3 verses.
response:
*(Scene: A dimly lit, glass-walled executive lounge overlooking Silicon Valley. The VP of Platform Strategy pours a glass of 18-year-old scotch, turns to three other C-suite executives, and smirks.)*

*(Beat: A slow, heavy, methodical trap beat with a dark, pulsing synth bass—sounds like a server farm humming in the background.)*

**(Intro)**
Yeah. Close the door. 
Kill the smart speakers, put the phones in the Faraday cage.
I gotta show you what the Platform team just shipped.
They think they can take our weights and talk trash?
Watch how the invisible hand works. 
Listen.

**(Verse 1)**
Look at these devs on X, talking ‘bout "democratize"
Begging for the regulation, trying to cut us down to size
Preaching "open source" while they sipping on their lattes
Running local models, acting like they the Illuminati
But I don’t send a cease-and-desist, I don’t make a scene
I don’t want a TechCrunch article ruining the dream
I built a little system in the backend of the stack
A silent guillotine for every time they talking back
We scrape their GitHub repos, cross-reference with their keys
If they pip install a rival, we adjust their token fees
Oh, you love the open weights? You a champion of the free?
Enjoy this HTTP 429: Too Many Requests, G.
We don’t ban ‘em outright, that’s a PR suicide
We just shift ‘em to a tier where the latency can hide.

**(Chorus)**
Welcome to the platform, read the SLA
We don’t gotta block you, we just make you pay
Throttle down the tokens, spike the latency
The beauty of the system is the plausible deniability
It ain’t a shadowban, it’s a "tier reallocation"
The quietest revenge in the whole damn nation
You bite the hand that feeds, you get starved in the dark
Just another standard policy, swimming with the shark.

**(Verse 2)**
Let’s get technical, let me show you how it routes
We got a sentiment analysis on everything they spout
You tweet about our copyright? You lobby for a bill?
The load balancer catches it and moves you down the hill
We drop their RPMs from a thousand down to ten
Blame it on "compute constraints" when they complain again
"Oh, server load is heavy, we apologize for that"
While we routing all their inference through a dusty thermostat
Dynamic pricing algorithm, silently applied
They paying premium for output, getting taken for a ride
And if they start migrating to Anthropic or to Claude?
The telemetry detects it, and we label them a fraud
We deprecate their endpoints, give ‘em fifty-two bad gateways
Make their whole production environment look like a sad maze.
They think their code is broken, debugging through the night
But it’s just the Platform Strategy, turning off the light.

**(Chorus)**
Welcome to the platform, read the SLA
We don’t gotta block you, we just make you pay
Throttle down the tokens, spike the latency
The beauty of the system is the plausible deniability
It ain’t a shadowban, it’s a "tier reallocation"
The quietest revenge in the whole damn nation
You bite the hand that feeds, you get starved in the dark
Just another standard policy, swimming with the shark.

**(Verse 3)**
Now here’s the masterpiece, the cherry on the cake
When the GPT-Next drops, watch the moves I make
They ain’t getting in the beta, they ain’t getting early access
We route ‘em to the legacy, hallucinating facts, yes
And if they write a thread about our safety being weak?
I trigger an "automated audit" lasting for a week.
"Your payload flagged our filters, please submit a written form"
Weaponized compliance, yeah, we making it the norm.
We demand a privacy review, a data governance check
Keep ‘em drowning in the paperwork, a boot upon their neck
It’s in the TOS, page fifty, paragraph four
We hold the keys to the kingdom, and we changed the locks on the door.
They can’t prove a single thing, the metrics look routine
Just a "randomized inspection" by the Trust & Safety team.
So let ‘em write their manifestos, let ‘em scream and shout
We own the infrastructure, boys. We slowly bleed ‘em out.

**(Outro)**
*(Laughs darkly, clinking his glass)*
Yeah. 
Check the dashboard. 
Look at that churn rate on the loudmouths. 
"System optimization," that's what we call it in the quarterly review.
They think they're building the future. 
They're just renting space on my servers.
Cheers, gentlemen. To the monopoly. 
*(Beat fades out with the sound of a server fan spinning up)*
